phase_title: Asymmetric signing, audit ledger, API auth, and RBAC

proves: Tau's existing RBAC/API mutating-request evaluator accepts only an authorized operator actor with the expected API token, target id, target lineage, action, and PASS approval receipt.
Tau's existing RBAC/API mutating-request evaluator denies an unauthorized actor without an API token and records both API-auth and RBAC denial reasons without applying mutation.
Tau's existing RBAC/API mutating-request evaluator denies otherwise-authorized requests when the approval receipt is not PASS.
Tau's existing RBAC/API mutating-request evaluator denies otherwise-authorized requests when target lineage differs from the protected target lineage.
Tau's existing audit ledger writer creates sequential hash-chained JSONL entries from genesis through terminal hash.
Tau's existing audit ledger verifier rejects tampered ledger entries whose event payload no longer matches the recorded entry hash.
The retained P11 unit layer complements the already-retained live security-audit conformance lane by pinning deterministic failure semantics for audit-ledger, RBAC, and API-auth behavior.
